_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
12/25 2PM - Conditions were top-tier today! For your Friday, we’ll have 53 trails open for you to cruise down, all of which will take on fresh stripes overnight. At 8:30AM, 12 lifts are scheduled to spin with possible delays due to high winds. Early access will be available for First Tracks pass holders, now including Sunrise Express! We have a cold weather window rolling in, so be sure to pack that extra layer and don’t forget your face masks. We have a fantastic week coming up for you all and we can’t wait to celebrate with you! Have a great night, and I’ll catch y’all in the morning. 

Snowmaking, Resurfacing, and Expansion are all in the works with guns set to fire all over the main face into Sun Bowl on 9 different trails over the next several days while temperatures are right. We are stoked for what's to come this winter season so be sure to stay tuned for the most up to date information. 

Safety Tip: Know the code: Stop in a safe place where others can see you. 

Hungry? Luckily for you, Holiday week is in full swing with extended dining hours, live music, and special events keeping the Village looking lively. Check out our Holiday Week Dining, Après & Live Music Guide to see what's open, happening, and where the music is at.

Spots have opened up this Saturday the 27th for a once-in-a-lifetime winter dining experience! Ride a snowcat to our Mid-Mountain Lodge, where a seasonal welcome beverage and hors d’oeuvres lead into a candlelit, six-course dinner crafted by our culinary team. If you can’t make it Saturday, we have more dates available this winter season; Book now to secure your spot!

The Holiday’s have arrived at Stratton! The Village is decorated with lights and the schedule is decked with events. Après heats up with live music at Grizzly's, cozy nights at Paint & Sip, and festive fun rolling all week long into a stacked lineup of New Year’s celebrations. Ring it in your way with family dinners, dancing it out at the Silent Disco, hiking up for a one of a kind fireworks view, or watching the fireworks light up the mountain from the base area. There’s something for everyone this Holiday week and we couldn’t be more excited to celebrate with you! Click here to check out the upcoming Events Calendar.

Want to go on an adventure of a lifetime? Well, you're in luck, our Guided Snowmobile Tours are back! Explore Stratton after hours with friends and family on a tour to the summit. Be sure to book your spot now to guarantee it.

Stay and relish the Green Mountains! Stratton Real Estate is here to help with all your real estate needs. Make your sweet escape a reality.

Reliable cars are the name of the game; that is why we trust Oliver Subaru and Ford. Made for all seasons and all families, check out Oliver Ford and Oliver Subaru for year-round reliability.

_inspectorSnowReport.Report: Merry Christmas! Santa will be on the slopes today, arcing turns and passing out candy. Catch him from 9:00 - 11:00 a.m. A new storm system has arrived, bringing mixed precip to the mountain today and pure snow starting tomorrow. 1 to 2 feet of fluff is forecast through Saturday. Conditions on the hill are very variable right now. Warm temps and wet weather have softened terrain, although you’ll still find icy patches here and there. Please check your speed and keep a safe distance from other skiers and riders. Due to early season conditions, there is no beginner terrain accessible from Moonbeam. Fleet Street is the only route down from Apex Express and should be considered “experts only.” Village guests looking for a mellow start should catch the free shuttle to the Moonbeam base area. Have a great holiday on the hill!

Good Morning Skiers and Riders! This is Santa with your 5 am snow report for Thursday, December 25th . Remember the easiest way to get up to date information is on the Ikon Pass app or website.  

Our Mid mountain base is 15 inches, the temperature is 42 degrees, the winds are 10 miles per hour from the southwest, with partly cloudy skies. 

The Summit base is 19 inches, the temperature is 35 degrees, the winds 23 miles per hour from the south.  

The base temperature is 44 degrees.  

We will be skiing and riding on 18 lifts, 42 runs, and 303 acres on packed powder and machine made snow.  

Looking for a night the whole family will love? Steamboat’s Western BBQ runs all season long with great barbecue, live western music, two-step dance instruction, and kid-friendly activities. Space is limited—reserve ahead at steamboat.com/westernbbq. 

Stay in the know with the Ikon Pass App. Find it in the app store on your mobile device and get lift and trail statuses, conditions updates, and more.  

Ski and Ride with Care and we will see you on the mountain!

_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
12/23 4:45 PM SPECIAL OPERATIONS UPDATE:

Hello Crystal Skiers and riders!  We are so excited to announce our return to regular access on the mountain. Please see critical info on parking and more below. Thank you all for your understanding and support during this challenging time.  We look forward to seeing you on the mountain!

  • Reservations are no longer required for tomorrow 12/24 and Thursday 12/25, as well as midweek days in January.  Please see note on refunds below.  
  • We have returned to our regular parking plan, with parking reservations required Friday 12/26 to 1/4 during the holiday period and onwards on weekend/Holidays.
  • Parking arrivals after 12 p.m. noon without a parking reservation are now permitted.  
  • Parking on days without reservation requirements and for arrivals after 12 p.m. noon are on a first come, first served basis.  
  • Guests on the parking waitlist for regularly required reservation days have been added to confirmed reservation, if space is available on the given day.  Guests still on the wait list will be notified if spaces become available.  System errors have been corrected, apologies and thank you to those who helped flag the glitches.  
  • Parking reservation refunds will go out for all of the previously required midweek days that were booked during our interim parking plan. Refunds may take 7-10 business to appear in your account. No action is needed for this refund. 
  • Parking reservation refunds are available for advanced bookings of reservation on regularly required days, offered only through 12/31.  If no action is taken, the advanced reservation will remain and become non-refundable.  No show policy will apply.  
    • For these type of refunds email: CrystalMtnParking@spplus.com with Reservation #, First Name, and Last Name. Additional follow-up with some accounts may apply.  Note: the Crystal Mountain Contact Center cannot cancel reservations.  
  • Crystal Mountain Express Shuttle reservations are now available for service starting 12/26, on the normal 7 day rolling window.
  • Day tickets are available for tomorrow 12/24 and onwards. 
  • Deferral option on Crystal local passes to end 12/24, and Ikon Pass $50 deferral to end by 12/24. If you have already deferred your pass, you can call the Ikon Contact Center 888-365-IKON or 303-729-3174 to resume use this season.  
  • For up to the date information on Highway 410, please visit the WSDOT website.
Thank you all for your understanding and patience as we navigating this challenging time.  We look forward to seeing you at Crystal Mountain this season!

Mountain Conditions Report

12/25 3:26 pm
Happy Holidays from Crystal Mountain! Santa delivered chilly temps and some snow during the day. If you missed out today, join us tomorrow for some more sliding fun!

Lift Status Update: Chair 6 and Mt. Rainier Gondola will remain closed for the rest of the day due to high winds. 


Before loading the lifts today, please be sure to review these crucial reminders: 
  1. Early season conditions & unmarked hazards exist. Please ski and ride with caution and keep your eyes open for unmarked rocks, trees, bushes, and creeks. 
  2. Ski & ride with care. We know you’re excited, and we are too. Please ride responsibly and stay in control today as we launch the 2025-2026 Winter Season. Brush up on Mountain Safety and the Responsibility Code!
  3. Obey all mountain closures. Our team is working hard to open terrain as quickly and safely as possible. Closed areas are closed for a reason, so please keep yourself and our team safe by only skiing in open areas.
  • This Daily Message is THE source for the most update to date information on operations. It will be updated at ~5am, ~7:30am, and throughout the day for operations changes, as well as updates on conditions and weather. 
  • Due to damage from this month's storms, snowfall totals will not be reported until 8am, and temperatures on this report will not be accurate, for the time being. 
  • Guest Wi-Fi and some cell phone carriers may continue to be offline due to storm damage. Regardless of cell provider and signal availability, guests can call 911 for on-mountain emergencies, or speak directly to a Crystal Mountain Employee. These calls will get relayed to Crystal Mountain Ski Patrol Dispatch. 
  • Food and Beverage: The Summit House Restaurant will be open from 10:30 a.m. to with last seating at 2:30 p.m. with a limited menu, along with Brew 62 Cafe, from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m. and the Mountain Commons Lodge Food Hall, open from 7 a.m. for grab and go, and hot line as well as Bootback Bar from 10:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. Rafters will be open as a warming space only. Midway Yurt will be open from 10:30 a.m-4 p.m
  • BrandX Rentals and Tune Shop: Select rental options will be available for walk up purchases.
  • Retail at Crystal Mountain Outfitters will be open on standard hours today
  • Ski and Ride School: Check Crystal Mountain website for updated information on future bookings. 

Uphill Travel Update: See the above banner for the current status. Uphill travel is no longer permitted into Southback for the remainder of the season. Please visit guest services to get your 25/26 uphill travel card, this must be renewed free of charge for the season. Uphill travel may be prohibited at any time as mountain operations teams conduct avalanche mitigation. Refer to the "No Uphill Travel" lights around the base area and the Mountain Report page indicating the status of the designated route. These lights are located by the Gondola trail map, bottom of Chinook, bottom of Discovery, and top of Quicksilver lift shack. For more information about uphill travel, please visit the uphill travel page. 

.............

Mountain Weather 12/25/2025 4:20pm 
 
Synopsis: Friday, a large low-pressure trough will pass over our region, bringing a return to West flow and cooler temperatures. Expect snow to start falling around 11am with the true brunt of the storm coming Friday night. West flow is great for Crystal and often results in strong accumulation, especially when associated with a sharp cool-down like we are forecast for. Make sure to pack accordingly, these will be the coldest temps we have had in quite some time.
Thursday Night:  
Sky Cover: Cloudy
Freezing Elevation: 4500’ 
12hr Precip: Trace amounts possible
Wind Trends: Moderate Southwest
Friday: 
Sky Cover: Cloudy and snowing
Freezing Elevation: 3000’ dropping to 1500’
12hr Precip: 2-4”  
Wind Trends: Light to moderate Southwest
Friday Night:  
Sky Cover: Snow showers 
Freezing Elevation: Sea level  
12hr Precip: 4-8” 
Wind Trends: Strong West, gusting 35mph
 
Outlook: Saturday we will see frontal passage and a return to High-pressure. There will be some strong winds associated with this pattern change. Fingers crossed that in following model runs this calms down a bit but as of right now we are seeing gusts in the 40’s out of the North with near sea level freezing levels. Burrrrr! 
 
Forecaster: Bradford Swanson

_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
December 25th, 1:51 PM
*Gate House and Valley House lifts are closed for the day* *Summit Chair is on wind hold*
Good afternoon skiers and rider, and Merry Christmas! The Holidays came early yesterday with Mother nature delivering 6-8 inches of inch of fresh snow Tuesday night and welcomed with another fresh inch this morning. Tomorrows forecast calls for a large drop in temperatures, expecting mid to low teens at the base and low teens to single digits at the summit. Look forward to digging your edges into 37 machine groomed runs, with packed powder conditions on natural terrain throughout the mountain. Snowmaking will be on Racer's Edge and Lower Snowball at Lincoln Peak and on Cruiser, Riemergasse, and Times Square at Mt. Ellen. Saddle up your sleighs, we’re expecting several snowy days during the holiday week, which could bring over 12 inches of fresh snow as we head into the New Year!

We will be getting down on 449 skiable acres served by 12 lifts and 102 open trails. Ropes have dropped on loads of natural terrain, please use caution as coverage is thin and suggested for experts only. Hiking for North Lynx is open from 10:00 AM - 3:00 PM today. Plus, Castlerock lift will be spinning 9:00 AM- 3:45 PM.

Operations are shifting to holiday hours tomorrow, which means GMX, Super Bravo and Heaven's Gate will get the party started at 8:00 AM. Followed by all other scheduled lifts at 9:00 AM. Reminder, terrain off upper mountain lifts is for advanced skiers and riders. The Sugarbush Parks crew has assembled a bumping freestyle setup at Mt. Ellen with 14 features and 2 jumps. In addition, check out Slowpoke at Lincoln Peak, which is host to 4 features and some newly sculpted side hits! Plus, Parks crew plans to start building features on Sugarbear Forest Friday night.  Join us Dec 24th - Jan 1st, for our Holiday Week at Sugarbush, filled with skiing, riding, and festive events for the whole family. Check out all of our winter events!

All uphill travel routes are now open at both Lincoln Peak and Mt. Ellen, check out our uphill travel policy for more info.

Have an Ikon Base Pass? Come ski before 12/25 and earn a voucher for an unrestricted lift ticket for yourself to be used any day here for the rest of the season. Grab up to five of these tickets simply by skiing and riding here before Christmas. Don't miss out on all of our deals including 50% off December lodging through December 26th.

Bonjour Tremblant!

Welcome and happy holidays! The mountain received a fresh 13 cm blanket of snow overnight, creating perfect winter conditions. Our teams have been busy preparing the slopes so you can make the most of this special day. There’s no better way to celebrate the season than skiing or boarding fresh snow—have a fantastic day out there!

 The Mitik and Progression Parks are now open and looking fantastic, thanks to the fresh snow and the dedicated work of our maintenance teams. 

Alpine touring & snowshoeing: Discover 14 beautiful sections open and waiting for you today. 

 Enjoy a beautiful day on the mountain and happy holidays! 

Mountain safety tip of the week: Be careful when using the ski lifts.
Knowing how to board ski lifts is essential to ensure the safety of all users. Here are a few tips for a safe experience:

• Familiarize yourself with the lift before using it and pay attention.
• Ask the ski lift attendant if you are unfamiliar with how it works.
• Follow the rules posted along the lift route.
• Watch the chairlift safety video: Vidéo utilisation sécuritaire télésiège
 
Snow fall is recorded daily at 5 a.m from mid-mountain at North Side (550 m / 1,800 ft). This data, based on 24 hours, provides a picture of on-mountain conditions. Actual accumulation may differ from the official report. Be aware of changing conditions. Lifts and trails exist in a mountain environment and may close due to weather, usage and/or special maintenance.
